title: midshift-kernel-garden-notes-taylor-nguyen
content:
Midshift kernel garden — quick brain-dump (tomato patch approach)

Goal: keep a small, maintainable list for the midshift handoff. Not a playbook, just the noises I ran into and what I want to try next.

Today summary (what I observed)
- Intermittent p99 spikes on small-v1 model during steady-state QPS (12–20 q/s). p50 stable (~5-6ms), p99 oscillating between 95ms and 180ms depending on request shape.
- Noticed increased CPU ops on host when KV cache hit rate is low (~cache misses correlate with spikes).
- One concrete kernel-ish crash (segfault) from nvml memory observer while running multi-session local repro. Filed RINF-3321.

Quick repro notes (local)
- Command: ./bench --model small-v1 --seq 512 --qps 15 --concurrency 8 --kv-cache-enabled true
- Observed: p50: 4.9ms, p95: 34ms, p99: 128ms (switches to ~170ms once cache miss chain happens)
- Repro tip: seq variance matters — run a mixed length workload (64/256/512) to trigger the bad tail.

Hypotheses (brainstorm)
1) KV cache eviction + async refill is causing head-of-line stalls for some sessions. If refill runs on main executor, we might get skewed scheduling and spikes.
2) Prefetching logic uses a lock that contends under bursty misses. Lock hold time increases with disk/quantization decode latency.
3) Kernel: occasional de-synchronization between CUDA stream handling and our custom allocator leading to transient serialization.
4) NVML observer crash is unrelated but increases GC pressure as process restarts — need to confirm.

Things to try (short actionable tasks)
- [ ] Add micro-instrumentation around KV cache refill path (measure locks, time spent, thread affinity). Keep it low-overhead. (follow-up: internal perf PR)
- [ ] Run kernel build with NVTX markers and reproduce with nvprof to capture where the schedule stalls (target: reproduction under 10–15 min).
- [ ] Increase prefetch worker pool from 2 -> 4 on a canary host and run the mixed-length bench for 30 minutes (compare p99).
- [ ] Swap the custom allocator for jemalloc on a single node to see if it changes pacing (quick A/B).
- [ ] Add an early-return path on cache refill if session has already been served to avoid wasted work.

Notes for triage (context for whoever picks it up)
- RINF-3321: Segfault stack is noisy; top frames show nvml observer -> runtime init -> cudaStreamSynchronize. Crash does not reproduce locally 100% — only after ~3+ hours of load on the canary.
- PR 1493 touches KV prefetch scheduling; might interact with this. Keep an eye on that when landing.
- Slack: pinged #runtime-oncall with a short summary and a link to the local bench artifacts.

Quick checklist (what I actually changed today)
- instrumented timer in cache refill (lightweight) and pushed branch tng/instr-kv-refill -> TODO: open PR 1498
- ran quick local bench with prefetch pool 4; saw p99 drop from 128ms to ~95ms in a 10-minute run (promising but noisy)
- collected nvprof traces (saving to /tmp/nvprof-taylor-03-12) — need to scrub and upload to GH artifact storage

Open questions (notes-to-self)
- Is there a global backpressure metric from serving runtime we can expose per-session? Would help correlate which sessions trigger refill storms.
- How to trigger the nvml observer crash reliably? Could be memory fragmentation over time + specific sequence shapes.
- If cache refill is offloaded to background, what's the acceptable memory overhead for prefetch buffers? Need a safe default.

Hand-off snippets (for next shift)
- If you see p99 > 120ms for small-v1, run: ./bench --model small-v1 --seq 512 --qps 15 --concurrency 8 --mix-length true and let it run 20m. Attach perf log.
- If nvml segfault appears, do NOT hot-restart the host; collect core + nvprof logs, then escalate to SRE if host unstable.

Notes / random thought seeds
- Maybe we can use a leaky-bucket per-session for prefetch work to avoid burst storms.
- Consider async refill returning a future that is 'best-effort' — if session completes, future is cancelled and work discarded earlier.
- Could quantify "wasted prefetch" by tracking prefetch start time vs session last-request. Add metric: prefetch_wasted_count.

Next actions (priority ordering)
1) Finish PR for instrumentation (tng/instr-kv-refill) and get quick review from Anika.
2) Run a longer 2-hour canary with prefetch pool = 4, collect p50/p95/p99 + allocator stats.
3) Investigate allocator swap to see if fragmentation plays into nvml observer issue.
4) Draft a short blameless incident note if nvml segfault recurs so we have a record for SRE/infra.

Small TODOs (personal)
- [ ] Upload nvprof traces to GH artifact and link in RINF-3321.
- [ ] Remind Diego to rerun PR 1493 benchmarks after landing.
- [ ] Write a one-paragraph summary for the 10am handoff channel.

End of midshift notes — leaving the garden a bit damp, tomato seedlings look ok. 

-- Taylor
